event.title: Alberta votes on non-binding separation question
event.what_happened: Albertans are voting on a provincial choice question asking whether Alberta should remain a province of Canada or whether the provincial government should begin the legal process for a later binding provincial referendum on separation from Canada.
event.event_type: non-binding provincial referendum vote on a future separation process
event.event_date_basis: Packet 1 says, "People in the province of Alberta head to the polls on Monday," and Packet 1 was published on 2026-10-19; Packet 4 also says, "please vote ... on October 19th."

latest_development.summary: Voting is underway in Alberta on the non-binding separation question. Ballots are to be counted by hand beginning no earlier than 20:00 local time on Monday, with the separation-question results expected in the early hours of Tuesday.

confirmed_facts.fact: On 2026-10-19, Albertans are voting on whether Alberta should remain a province of Canada or whether the government should begin the legal process for a future binding provincial referendum on separation.
The Oct. 19 vote itself is non-binding.
Question 10, the separation choice question, will be counted first, and ballots are being counted by hand.
Officials have said ballot counting will begin no earlier than 20:00 local time on Monday.
Officials have said results on the separation question should be available in the early hours of Tuesday.
Danielle Smith called the vote earlier in 2026 after a petition gathered about 300,000 signatures asking for a binding referendum on separation.
Another petition opposing separation was signed by more than 400,000 people.
Danielle Smith opposes separation, and Al Jazeera reported that on 2026-10-14 she said she had voted against seceding.
Prime Minister Mark Carney urged Albertans to vote against separation at a rally in Edmonton on Thursday, 2026-10-15.
There are nine other referendum questions on the ballot besides the separation question.

For Question 10, the referendum period began.
Danielle Smith announced she had voted against seceding, according to Al Jazeera.
Mark Carney campaigned against separation at a rally in Edmonton.
Albertans head to the polls on the non-binding separation question and nine other referendum questions.
Hand counting is set to begin no earlier than 20:00 local time, with Question 10 counted first.
Officials have said the separation-question results should be available in the early hours of Tuesday.

background.fact: 2026-03-31: Alberta was in a referendum period; 2026-05-28: the referendum period for Question 10 began.
Earlier in 2026, Danielle Smith called the vote after a pro-separation petition gathered about 300,000 signatures.

Before the vote, a court blocked the pro-separation petition / found a binding referendum on separation could not proceed without consultation with First Nations; the Alberta government says it is appealing.
2026-10-14: Smith said she had voted against seceding.
2026-10-15: Carney spoke at a 'Forever Canadian' rally in Edmonton urging a vote against separation.

legal.statement: Albertans are voting on a non-binding choice question asking whether Alberta should remain a province of Canada or whether the government should begin the legal process required under the Canadian Constitution to hold a binding provincial referendum on separation.
If the option to begin the process for a future binding referendum receives majority support, the government says it would start the legal processes necessary to hold that later binding referendum.
A court ruling found that a binding referendum on separation could not be held without a constitutionally mandated consultation process with First Nations on effects on treaty rights.
Elections Alberta says O.C. 160/2026 orders that the results of Question 10 are not binding.

lifecycle.event: Alberta referendum vote on whether to begin the process for a future binding separation referendum
lifecycle.notes: Counting is by hand. Question 10 is to be counted first. Packet 1 says counting starts no earlier than 20:00 local on Monday.

reconciled.discrepancy: Some reports frame Monday's ballot as a separation referendum, while others describe it as only a step toward a future referendum.
reconciled.resolution: The Oct. 19 vote itself is non-binding. It asks voters to choose between remaining in Canada and starting the legal process for a later binding provincial referendum on separation.
reconciled.resolved_by: Packets 4 and 5, supported by Packet 1's quoted ballot text.

reconciled.discrepancy: Packet 1 says a court blocked the pro-separation petition; Packet 4 says a court found a binding referendum could not be held without First Nations consultation.
reconciled.resolution: These descriptions are compatible: the court ruling impeded the original binding-referendum route, and the government proceeded with a non-binding Question 10 instead.

unverified: Fox News reports, without primary sourcing in this packet set, that Danielle Smith told CBC News she would not hold another referendum on separation while she remains premier if most Albertans vote to stay.
Fox News reports that Alberta separatist leaders met Republican strategists in Calgary in January to examine support-mobilization software; no primary source is included here.
Fox News reports that separatist leaders suggested exchanging water and oil for U.S. support in meetings with State Department officials last year; no primary source is included here.
Cory Morgan's claim in Fox News that more than half of the UCP's nearly 55,000 members support Alberta independence is not independently established in this packet set.

angle: Albertans are voting Monday on a non-binding separation question that could start the legal process toward a later binding referendum; hand-counted results on the separation question are expected early Tuesday.
